why_paper: This site never holds your contacts, account numbers, policy numbers, medical details, the names of your doctors or your documents. Each worksheet is a blank form: print it and fill it in by hand. Nothing you write on one is typed into this site. Keep the paper copies where you would find them with the power and the network down.
why: This site never holds your contacts, account numbers, policy numbers, medical details, the names of your doctors or your documents. Each worksheet is a blank form. Signed in, you can open it as a file in your own Google Drive, in a folder called “Household Plan”: the site creates the blank copy, keeps the link to it, and never reads what you write. items: 1. From another device, sign in to the phone maker's finder, try to locate the phone and mark it as lost, which locks it.

blocks.note: Ask for the answers in writing. Leave room under each question.
fields: Water: does it reach my floor by street pressure, by pumps or from a roof tank?

Water: where is the building's main water valve, and who is allowed to close it? (Residents do not operate it.)

blocks.heading: When the alarm sounds
lines: Firefighters' instructions and any announcement come first, then your building's fire safety plan (HR-02).
If you have neither, use the rule the New York City Fire Department teaches.
Fire or smoke in your own home: get everyone out, close the door behind you, take the stairs, never the elevator, and call 911 from a safe place.

Fire somewhere else in a fire-resistive building (concrete or protected steel): it is usually safer to stay in your home with the door closed, call 911 with your floor and unit, and follow the cannot-leave steps (HR-07); leave if smoke or heat comes into your home or you are told to.
Fire somewhere else in a combustible building (wood frame): it is usually safer to leave at once.
Whenever you leave, feel the door and the handle first.
If the door is warm, do not open it.
If it is cool, open it slowly; if the hallway is clear, close every door behind you and walk down the nearest stairs to your meeting place.
Use your other stairwell only if the way to it is clear.
Never walk into a smoke-filled hallway or stairwell to leave a fire that is somewhere else: go back in, close the door and follow HR-07.

blocks.heading: If you cannot leave
lines: Stay in your unit, or go back to it, and close every door between you and the smoke.
Push wet towels or sheets into the gap around the door and over any vent where smoke comes in.
Call 911 and give the building address, your floor and unit number, and how many people are with you; keep in contact, because clearing a tall building can take a long time.
If smoke or flames are coming up the outside of the building from below you, keep the windows shut and signal through the glass with a flashlight.
Otherwise open a window a few inches and wave a bright cloth or a flashlight so crews can see where you are, and close it again if smoke comes in.
Never break a window, because you may need to close it.
Sources: New York City Fire Department; US Fire Administration. The rule and its sources are in action HR-06 on the site.

blocks.heading: Bleach
lines: Use the drinking-water directions printed on your own bottle if it has them: they are written for that exact strength.
If the label gives none, check that it is plain unscented bleach of 5% to 9% sodium hypochlorite and use CDC's table: 8 drops per gallon of clear water, or 2 drops per quart.
Double it if the water is cloudy, colored or very cold.
Stir and wait at least 30 minutes before drinking.
Bleach does not make water safe from fuel or chemicals.
Use the label's directions or CDC's table, never a mix of the two.

blocks.heading: Boiling
lines: Bring a pot of water to a rolling boil, where large bubbles keep breaking the surface, and hold it there for 1 full minute.
Above 5,000 feet, hold it for 3 minutes: that is EPA's figure, CDC prints 6,500 feet, and this site uses the lower one.
If the water is cloudy, let it settle and strain it through a clean cloth or coffee filter first.
Boiling does not make water safe from fuel or chemicals.

blocks.heading: The three kinds of water notice
lines: Boil-water notice: germs may be in the water.

For drinking, cooking, washing food, making ice, brushing teeth and pets' bowls, use bottled water, or tap water held at a rolling boil for as long as your notice says and cooled, even if it has been through a filter jug; if the notice gives no time, 1 minute (3 minutes above 5,000 feet).
For a formula-fed baby, CDC says to use ready-to-feed formula if you can.
Adults can shower, taking care not to swallow any water; give babies and small children a sponge bath.

Do-not-drink notice: a chemical or toxin may be in the water and boiling will not make it safe, so use bottled water for drinking, cooking, washing fruit and vegetables, ice, brushing teeth, formula and pets.
Do-not-use notice: touching the water may be dangerous, so use bottled water for everything and follow the utility.
Under any notice, do not use the water or ice dispenser in a refrigerator, and ask the utility whether tap water you stored before the notice is safe.
